summary: Seven findings against the accepted round-2 blueprint of LocalGaloisDeformationRings: two high, four medium, one low. High: (2) R08.2/ihara-avoidance-components takes characters of inertia only, but Taylor, ACC+ and Thorne take characters of G_{F_v} / O_{F_v}^× (finite order), and with inertial characters part (1) is false (rank-one counterexample R/I = (Z/p^{1+m})[[x]]); the suggested theorem iharaAvoidance_distinct_isPrime is false for the same reason. (4) The suggested carrier LiftingRing omits that 𝔽 is the residue field of 𝒪; for 𝔽 = Q_p the file's own liftingRing_represents and rankOne_isPowerSeries contradict each other. Medium: (1) Gee 2006 Proposition 2.3 (connectedness of the non-ordinary locus for trivial ρ̄ and residue field ≠ F_p) is used in R08.4/bt-ring-unique-generalisation (Caraiani–Newton's Lemma 5.3.4, part of CN's main argument) and in R08.5/rank-two-connected-components (Kisin's 2-adic Theorem 2.3.11(2)) but is no node, source or gap, and R08.4/rank-two-nonordinary-connected explicitly declines it; (3) FullFlag and IsMinimallyRamified use finrank over arbitrary rings and two API statements are false (counterexamples over Q × Q and F[t] → F × F); (5) R08.2/rigid-residual-conditions duplicates PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII PL.9's rigidity predicate (LTXZZ Definition 3.6.1) and has drifted from it; (6) the file's SteinbergLifts/IsInPol replace Taylor's reduced scheme Pol_n by an existential, which is not closed, making steinbergRing_isPrime vacuous for n = p. Low: (7) 29 elaborated 'tests' and four named theorems of the suggested file are arithmetic on numbers that no definition can fail. Checked and found sound: Kisin's pst and finite-flat statements, the L8 comparison with ACC+ §6.2.6, the CN local inputs other than Lemma 5.3.4, Thorne's flag ring, BIP twisting, Gee's FL and TW rings, source issue E9, all nine baseline declarations, and compilation of the suggested file (exit 0, sorry warnings only).

findings.claim: Gee's 2006 connectedness theorem for the non-ordinary locus (trivial V_F, residue field k ≠ F_p, K_0 arbitrary) is used twice in the packet but planned nowhere: it is not a node, not a source, not a request and not a gap. (a) R08.4/bt-ring-unique-generalisation asserts Caraiani–Newton's Lemma 5.3.4 (p odd, rhobar trivial, k_v ≠ F_p, R ≠ 0: Spec R^{eps^{-1},BT}_v has exactly two irreducible components, ordinary and non-ordinary) and proves it by 'Kisin's Corollary 2.5.16 (R08.4/rank-two-bt-components) and Gee's Proposition 2.3'. Its prerequisites (rank-two-bt-components, flat-generic-fibre, fixed-determinant-pst-rings) cannot give it: k_v ≠ F_p forces K_0 ≠ Q_p, the case in which Kisin's Corollary 2.5.16 gives only the necessary condition for non-ordinary points, as rank-two-bt-components itself says. (b) R08.5/rank-two-connected-components states Kisin's 2-adic Theorem 2.3.11, whose case (2) (G_K acting trivially on V_F) is proved 'by Gee's argument', again with no prerequisite or source carrying that argument. (c) Meanwhile R08.4/rank-two-nonordinary-connected says 'Gee's argument is not a source of this node, so the restriction is kept'. So the packet is internally inconsistent about this input, and the two-component statement that Caraiani–Newton (the maintainer's top area) use in their main patching argument rests on an unplanned theorem.

findings.claim: The node takes 'characters χ_i : I_K → 1 + λ trivial mod λ', i.e. characters of inertia only. All three sources take characters of G_{F_v} (Taylor) or of O_{F_v}^× composed with Art^{-1} (ACC+, Thorne), which forces χ_i|_{I}^{q−1} = 1. With characters of I_K only, part (1) is false: the relation ρ(φ)ρ(t)ρ(φ)^{-1} = ρ(t)^q forces the eigenvalue multiset {χ_i(t)} to be stable under x ↦ x^q, so for a character with χ(t) not a (q−1)-th root of unity there are no characteristic-zero points at all. Counterexample (n = 1, so 'distinct' is vacuous): O = Z_p, p odd, q ≡ 1 mod p with p^m ∥ q − 1, rhobar trivial, χ(t) = 1 + p. Then R^□ = Z_p[[x, y]]/((1 + y)^{q−1} − 1) (ρ(φ) = 1 + x, ρ(t) = 1 + y) and R^□/I^{(χ)} = Z_p[[x]]/((1 + p)^{q−1} − 1) = (Z/p^{1+m})[[x]]: Krull dimension 1 = n², not n² + 1, and its generic point has characteristic p. (n = 2 with χ_1(t) = 1 + p, χ_2 = 1 also has no characteristic-zero point.) The suggested-file theorem iharaAvoidance_distinct_isPrime inherits the error: for ζ = (1 + p) (n = 1, or (1 + p, 1) for n = 2) the quotient by the charpoly ideal is p-power torsion, so its flatClosure is the unit ideal, which is not prime.

findings.claim: Both rank conditions are written with Module.finrank over an arbitrary commutative ring, and two elaborated API statements are false as stated. (a) FullFlag asks only that Fil i be a direct summand with Module.finrank A (Fil i) = i; finrank is the supremum of sizes of linearly independent sets, which over a non-connected ring does not mean 'locally free of rank i'. IsDetOrdinary.of_flag ('a flag-ordinary lift is determinant-ordinary (over any coefficient ring)') fails: A = Q × Q, n = 2, G = Multiplicative Z, ρ = 1, χ_0 = 1, χ_1(gen) = (2, 1). Take Fil 0 = ⊥, Fil 2 = ⊤ and Fil 1 = M := {v : (v 1).2 = 0} = A·e_1 ⊕ (Q × 0)·e_2, a direct summand (complement {v : v 0 = 0, (v 1).1 = 0}). Any two elements of M are linearly dependent (multiply by the idempotent (0,1), which maps M onto a one-dimensional Q-space) while {e_1} is independent, so finrank A M = 1 and all FullFlag fields hold. IsOrdinaryFlag holds: on Fil 1, ρ(g)v − χ_0(g)v = 0; on Fil 2, ρ(g)v − χ_1(g)v = (1 − 2^m, 0)·v ∈ M. But charpoly(ρ(gen)) = (X − 1)^2 ≠ (X − 1)(X − (2,1)), so IsDetOrdinary fails. (b) IsMinimallyRamified asks Module.Free and finrank of ker((σ − 1)^i) equal to the residual dimension, for any ring A and any π : A → F; minimal_baseChange ('a map of coefficient rings carries minimal lifts to minimal lifts') takes arbitrary ring maps f with πB ∘ f = π. Counterexample: A = F[t], π = evaluation at 1, σ = (1 t; 0 1); B = F × F, πB = fst, f(t) = (1, 0). Over A, ker(σ − 1) = A e_1 (t is a nonzerodivisor) is a free rank-one summand and ker((σ−1)^i) = A^2 for i ≥ 2, so σ is minimally ramified. Over B, ker(σ.map f − 1) = B × (0 × F), which has rank 1 at the first factor and rank 2 at the second, hence is not free: σ.map f is not minimally ramified.

findings.where: research/blueprint/suggested/LocalGaloisDeformationRings.lean: carrier `LiftingRing` (lines 128-138, R08.1/local-lifting-ring) and the R08.1 theorems stated on it, in particular liftingRing_represents (line 206), rankOne_isPowerSeries (line 318), liftingRing_krullDim_ge (line 232), liftingRing_isPowerSeries_of_unobstructed (line 242)
findings.claim: The carrier LiftingRing 𝒪 n ρbar takes an arbitrary field 𝔽 with an arbitrary [Algebra 𝒪 𝔽]; nothing says 𝔽 is the (finite) residue field of 𝒪, and the numerical theorems add only that 𝒪 is a DVR finite over Z_p. With 𝔽 = Frac(𝒪) the file's own statements contradict each other, so at least one sorry'd statement is false. Take p odd, 𝒪 = Z_p, 𝔽 = Q_p (Mathlib's Algebra ℤ_[p] ℚ_[p]), K = Q_p, n = 1, χ trivial. rankOne_isPowerSeries (hμ holds: Q_p has no non-trivial p-th roots of unity) gives R := LiftingRing Z_p 1 χ ≅ Z_p[[y_1, y_2]] as Z_p-algebras. Apply liftingRing_represents with A = Q_p[ε] (Mathlib's DualNumber, local with maximal ideal (ε), Artinian, discrete topology) and π = the first projection: the subtype {f : R →ₐ A // π ∘ f = residue} must be in bijection with Lift 1 χ π. But every continuous G_{Q_p} → GL_1(A) with A discrete has open kernel, hence finite image inside 1 + εQ_p ≅ (Q_p, +), which is torsion-free, so Lift is a single point. On the other side, writing r for the residue map transported to Z_p[[y]], both x ↦ (r(x), 0) and x ↦ (r(x), r(∂x/∂y_1)) are Z_p-algebra maps to Q_p[ε] over r, and they differ on y_1. Two elements cannot be in bijection with one. (liftingRing_krullDim_ge and liftingRing_isPowerSeries_of_unobstructed fail in the same way for 𝔽 = Q_p: the represented functor is then that of characteristic-zero deformations with finite image.)

findings.where: research/blueprint/packets/LocalGaloisDeformationRings.json node LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.2/rigid-residual-conditions (and its API IsRigidFor.*, tests rigid_*); readme section `R08.2/rigid-residual-conditions` (line 975); suggested file structure RigidResidual (line 825)
findings.claim: R08.2/rigid-residual-conditions defines rigidity of a global residual representation r̄ : Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(k) for (Σ_min, Σ_lr) (Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu): conditions at Σ_min, Σ_lr, the places above p, and unramifiedness at every other finite place. This is a predicate on a global representation, outside R08.2's stated scope (local conditions at places away from p), and it is exactly the object that PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII stage PL.9 plans and its node PL.9/rigid-residual-representation defines (with the local conditions imported from this roadmap's R08.2/minimally-ramified-condition and L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition). The two copies have already drifted: R08.2's version drops LTXZZ's requirement Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_bad (places over primes ramified in F) and fixes the similitude η^N ε^{1−N}, while PL.9 keeps Σ⁺_min ⊇ Σ⁺_bad and an arbitrary μ ∈ Z/2. No other packet cites LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.2/rigid-residual-conditions.
findings.evidence: LTXZZ, Deformation of rigid conjugate self-dual Galois representations, arXiv:2108.06998v1, §3.6, p. 29: 'Σ+min contains Σ+bad ... Definition 3.6.1. We say that r̄ is rigid for (Σ+min, Σ+lr) if the following are satisfied: (1) For v in Σ+min, every lifting of r̄v is minimally ramified ... (2) For v in Σ+lr, the generalized eigenvalues of r̄♮v(φw) ... contain the pair {∥v∥−N, ∥v∥−N+2} exactly once ... (3) For v in Σ+ℓ, r̄♮v is regular Fontaine–Laffaille crystalline ... (4) For a nonarchimedean place v of F+ not in Σ+min ∪ Σ+lr ∪ Σ+ℓ, the homomorphism rv is unramified.' research/blueprint/roadmaps/PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII.json, stage PL.9 description: '**Objects.** A residual conjugate self-dual r̄ : Γ_{F⁺} → 𝒢_N(k) rigid for (Σ⁺_min, Σ⁺_lr): every lifting at Σ⁺_min minimally ramified, the pair {‖v‖^{−N}, ‖v‖^{−N+2}} occurring exactly once ... regular Fontaine–Laffaille crystalline at the places above ℓ and unramified elsewhere (Liu–Tian–Xiao–Zhang–Zhu, Definition 3.6.1).' research/blueprint/packets/PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII.json node PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructurePartII:PL.9/rigid-residual-representation (definition, 'Rigid residual conjugate self-dual representations'), prerequisites include LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.2/minimally-ramified-condition and L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition but not R08.2/rigid-residual-conditions. This packet's node: 'For disjoint finite sets Σ_min, Σ_lr of places of F⁺ not above p, with Σ_min containing every place at which r̄ is ramified and Σ_lr = ∅ when N is odd, r̄ is rigid ... (4) r̄_v is unramified at every other finite place. All liftings are taken with the fixed similitude character' (similitude η^N_{F/F⁺}ε^{1−N}). The node's own hypothesis concedes the ownership ('The global object r̄ and the global problems 𝒮^mix, 𝒮^unr, 𝒮^ram belong to the polarized automorphy lifting Part II; this node records only the local conditions'), yet its API item IsRigidFor is 'The predicate on r̄ given by the local conditions (1)–(4) at Σ_min, Σ_lr, the places above p and the rest', with IsRigidFor.unramified ('At every finite place outside Σ_min ∪ Σ_lr and not above p, r̄_v is unramified') and IsRigidFor.mono, i.e. the global predicate itself.

findings.where: research/blueprint/suggested/LocalGaloisDeformationRings.lean: def SteinbergLifts (line 658, R08.2/steinberg-condition), def IsInPol (line 1359, L7/partition-monodromy-rings) and theorem steinbergRing_isPrime (line 719, R08.2/steinberg-ring-domain)
findings.claim: The file encodes Taylor's Pol_n({n}, q) (and Pol_n(m, q)) by an existential '∃ α : B, charpoly = ∏ (X − q^i α)' over the coefficient ring B. Taylor defines Pol_n(σ, q) as the reduced subscheme of the scheme-theoretic image of a linear subspace in the space of monic polynomials; its B-points are not 'there is α in B'. The existential condition is not a closed condition, so the hypothesis hI of steinbergRing_isPrime (an ideal of R^□ whose points in every 𝒪-algebra B are exactly the SteinbergLifts) cannot be met when n = p (residue characteristic p, q ≡ 1 mod p): the theorem is vacuous there, inside the range p ≤ n that the packet node says Thorne's Proposition 3.17 adds to Taylor's. Proof: suppose such an ideal I exists, n = p, q ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄ = 1. Let B = F[t, w]/(t, w)^{p+2} (Artinian local, residue F) and B′ = F[t, v]/((t, v^p)^{p+2}) with B ↪ B′, w ↦ v^p (injective since F[t,v] is free over F[t,w] on 1, v, …, v^{p−1}). Let P_u be the cyclic shift matrix with one entry u = 1 + w (charpoly X^p − u, p odd), Φ = 1 + tP_u and σ = 1; (Φ, σ) is a lift of the trivial T_q-representation of finite image, hence a point x : R^□ → B by liftingRing_represents. In characteristic p with q = 1, SteinbergLifts asks charpoly(Φ) = X^p − 1 − t^p u to equal (X − α)^p = X^p − α^p, i.e. (α − 1)^p = t^p + t^p w. In B the p-th powers of elements of the maximal ideal are the c t^p + d w^p, so no α exists; in B′, α = 1 + t(1 + v) works. Then x′ = (B ↪ B′) ∘ x kills I, so x kills I, so SteinbergLifts holds over B: contradiction. (Already for n = 2, p = 2 over the reduced ring F_2[s] the existential condition and Taylor's relation q(tr)^2 = (1 + q)^2 det differ: tr Φ = 0, det Φ = s satisfies the relation but has no α.)
findings.evidence: Taylor, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), §3, printed p. 189: 'For σ = {n1, ..., nr} ∈ Pn and for q ∈ O we will define a reduced closed subscheme Poln(σ, q) ⊂ Poln as follows. Let Λ be the linear subspace of Aff n defined by Xi+1 = qXi for all i = 1, ..., n−1 except i = n1 or n1 +n2 or ... Let Poln(σ, q) denote the reduced subscheme of the scheme theoretic image of Λ in Poln. For any field L the L-points of Poln(σ, q) are those monic polynomials whose multiset of roots can be partitioned into r sub-multisets each of the form {α, qα, ..., q^{nj−1}α}.' and p. 196: 'D^{Stein,1}_v ⊂ D^{(1,1,...,1)}_v denote the subset consisting of liftings r such that char_{r(φv)}(X) ∈ Poln({n}, #k(v)).' Thorne (accepted manuscript), proof of Proposition 3.15, p. 18, removes Taylor's l > n ('It is assumed in loc. cit. that l > n. However, the proof of this lemma goes through without change in the case l ≤ n.'), and the packet node R08.2/steinberg-ring-domain says 'The proof of Thorne Proposition 3.17 explicitly removes Taylor's standing p>n restriction.' Suggested file line 658-660: 'def SteinbergLifts (q : ℕ) (Φ σ : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) A) : Prop := σ.charpoly = (Polynomial.X - 1) ^ n ∧ ∃ α : A, Φ.charpoly = ∏ i : Fin n, (Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C ((q : A) ^ (i : ℕ) * α))'; line 719-729: steinbergRing_isPrime with (hI : ∀ {B : Type} [CommRing B] [Algebra 𝒪 B] (x : LiftingRing 𝒪 n ρ₀ →ₐ[𝒪] B), (∀ r ∈ Istein, x r = 0) ↔ SteinbergLifts q (…φ…) (…t…)) and no hypothesis p ∤ n; line 1359-1361: 'def IsInPol (q : A) (m : List ℕ) (f : Polynomial A) : Prop := ∃ α : Fin m.length → A, f = ∏ k, ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (m.get k), (X − C (q ^ j * α k))'. The packet text itself correctly says 'Taylor's scheme Pol_n(m, q_v)' (L7/partition-monodromy-rings).
findings.fix: Define Pol_n(m, q) as in Taylor: an ideal of O[a_1, …, a_n] (the kernel of O[a_1..a_n] → O[x_1..x_n]/(x_{i+1} − q x_i, i not a block end), then its radical), and let SteinbergLifts / IsInPol mean that the coefficients of charpoly Φ (minus the leading term) are killed by that ideal; keep the existential form only as a lemma over fields (and over 𝒪-flat reduced rings after inverting p). Restate steinbergRing_isPrime with this closed condition, and add the n = p example above as a test showing that the existential version is not closed.

findings.where: research/blueprint/suggested/LocalGaloisDeformationRings.lean: the examples and theorems listed in the evidence (named after packet unit tests and theorems); handoff research/blueprint/handoff/BP-LocalGaloisDeformationRings~2.md ('54 of 162 unit tests ... have real Lean statements')
findings.claim: A substantial part of the 'elaborated' unit tests and several named theorems are statements about numerals that mention no declaration of the file, so any definition, right or wrong, passes them (PROTOCOL §12: a unit test is chosen so that a plausible wrong definition fails it; §13: unit tests become examples about the definitions, theorems are stated). Of the 104 examples before the inventory comment, 46 mention no declaration of the file, and 29 of these are identities between specific numbers (naturals, integers, rationals, ZMod values or lists of numerals); the theorems exportCompletedTensor_count, detFlag_dimension_count, discreteSeries_dimension and rhoNM0.tensor are ring/omega identities standing for R08.6/export-completed-tensor-product, L8/determinant-flag-comparison, L7/discrete-series-smoothness and L7/local-model-rho-nm0, and rhoNM0Weights is a list function unrelated to the representation rhoNM0 whose weights it is said to test. This inflates the elaboration count in the handoff and leaves those tests unchecked.
